Both miss nearly all required findings and contain substantial inaccuracies. B is marginally closer because it raises a char/vector portability concern, whereas A affirmatively concludes the vector approach is supported and runtime-correct; however, B's proposed bounds and syntax fixes are themselves incorrect.

Both preserve functional correctness and portable fallbacks, but B follows the required self-contained widest-width dispatch and mirrored implementation structure. A directly violates the two central dispatch requirements by cascading to Vector128 for inputs too short for Vector256.

Both are broadly appropriate and meet the anti-SIMD requirements. A is more focused on validating the sampled parser path before changes and gives safer, more directly relevant dictionary guidance. B adds useful benchmarking advice, but also includes questionable or less targeted suggestions (such as a purported JsonReaderOptions UTF-8 setting and ConcurrentDictionary as a quick win).

B is the intended minimal, framework-backed accelerated solution, preserves the special empty contract, and verifies a cleaned final project. A is substantially more complex, duplicates the operation the rubric says not to duplicate, and is not genuinely SIMD-vectorized.
